content:
anya: Quick check — followup from yesterday's RFC: we're still undecided between doing aggressive attribute eviction at the gateway vs partitioning ingest by tenant for cost attribution. thoughts?

mike: TL;DR: eviction is simpler and cheaper to run, partitioning gives more accurate per-tenant queries but increases routing/ops complexity.

tariq: Real-world hit: we evicted a billing.customer_id once and billing shows up as 'unknown' for ~6h until rehydration — that triggered a billing support ticket. so fidelity matters for hot tenants. :grimacing:

lucy: Agree with tariq. Also partitioning helps when a small set of customers generate very high cardinality attributes (think huge metadata) — routing them to their own partitions prevents noisy tenants from inflating cold queries.

anya: Ops concern — partitioning multiplies the number of shards / streams we manage. autoscaling behavior becomes per-tenant instead of global. that could blow up cost if not gated.

mike: Tradeoffs matrix I sketched: 
- Eviction at gateway: low ingestion cost, smaller storage, risk of attribution loss for late-enriched attrs.
- Partition-by-tenant: high operational cost, accurate queries, easier chargeback.
- Hybrid (recommended): keep a small required set of billing attributes pinned, evict the rest; route top N noisy tenants into dedicated partitions.

tariq: Hybrid seems pragmatic. We should define "required set" concretely. My suggestion: [billing.customer_id, billing.key, tenant.id, service.name] and enforce proto-level validators to reject events missing them.

lucy: +1. Also add a soft TTL/eviction config so if a pinned attr isn't present you mark the trace as "attr-missing" rather than drop. That helps debugging.

anya: Example gateway config sketch: 

```
eviction:
  pinned_attrs: ["billing.customer_id", "tenant.id", "service.name"]
  max_other_attrs: 25
  missing_attr_behavior: "flag-notice"
routing:
  partition_threshold_tps: 2000
  dedicated_top_n: 50
```

mike: For the partitioning side, we need to decide routing key composition. tenant.id alone works for billing, but some customers share tenant across multiple orgs; maybe use tenant.id + billing.key. queries: will users run cross-partition joins? that's harder.

tariq: Cross-partition queries we proxy: fanout + merge at query layer for admin dashboards only. Not for real-time SLOs. That keeps common queries cheap.

ingest-bot: spike requested by @anya — creating task obs/ingest/attr-eviction-spike (link: https://phab.redwood/obs/EVCT-102).

anya: Next steps: mike + tariq pair on a short spike to: 1) implement pinned attr enforcement + flagging at gateway, 2) prototype per-tenant routing for top-20 noisy tenants, 3) generate cost delta estimate. Report back in 4 days. I'll own the RFC update.

lucy: I'll prepare a prompt set to validate we don't regress billing attribution in the quality checks.

mike: acked. I'll post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
